kpis.name: Registry entries at latest version
kpis.how: one exact GET /v0.1/servers/<name>/versions/latest per manifest name, compared with the release version. NOT a substring search: with 30,395 servers in the registry a search can push the exact match off page one, which is how this read 41 of 91 while a direct sample of 12 returned 12 of 12 present
kpis.why: The official registry is the index Claude, Cursor and VS Code pickers read.

kpis.name: Registry findable share
kpis.how: data/organic.json (name-substring search probes)
kpis.why: Search is name-only; a server nobody can find by the words they type does not exist.

kpis.name: Distribution surfaces live
kpis.how: data/distribution.json
kpis.why: Each free registry or catalog is a compounding source of installs.

kpis.name: URLs offered in the sitemap
kpis.how: curl mcp.zovo.one/sitemap.xml
kpis.why: Not a score to maximise. It was 312, of which 216 were client-by-product setup permutations measuring 73.6-77.5% similar to each other; Googlebot read the sitemap 7 times and then crawled 2 pages. Cut to 96 on 2026-09-07 and the permutations marked noindex,follow. See docs/SEO_INDEXATION_R1.md.

kpis.name: Google impressions, storefront
kpis.how: data/gsc.json, Search Console sc-domain:zovo.one filtered to //mcp.zovo.one/ pages, with a positive control on //zovo.one/ returning 63 clicks and 4,392 impressions to prove the filter works
kpis.why: Zero here across 99+ days means Google has never shown this site to anyone. It is the single most important organic number.

kpis.name: Named by a blind assistant
kpis.how: docs/BLIND_RECOMMENDATION_PROCEDURE.md: a subagent with no knowledge of this estate researches 18 frozen buyer-intent questions from data/blind_questions.json with web search and names the server it would recommend. Baseline run 2026-09-10 named 47 distinct MCP servers and none were ours.
kpis.why: The buyer does not browse a registry, they ask an assistant and install what it names. This is the only discovery number that maps to revenue.

kpis.name: Our share of recommendation citations
kpis.unit: of 18 questions where our host was cited at all
kpis.how: data/blind_recommendation_r1.json, host extracted from every URL the instrument cited. Baseline: github.com 21, glama.ai 7, ours 4, apify.com 4, mcpservers.org 3, registry.modelcontextprotocol.io 0. See docs/RECOMMENDATION_SOURCES_R1.md.
kpis.why: Separates a retrieval failure from a citation failure. Retrieved-but-not-cited is a content defect; never retrieved is an indexation defect. They have different fixes.

kpis.name: Repo clone-to-view ratio
kpis.how: data/baselines/loop33_baseline.json, gh api traffic/clones vs traffic/views. Baseline 2026-09-10: 3,410 clones from 502 unique clients against 54 views from 31 humans.
kpis.why: Not a score to maximise. It states who the repo front door is actually serving, which is machines by about 63 to 1, and it is why the repo is written for a reader that is mostly not a person.

kpis.name: Googlebot URL coverage
kpis.how: data/traffic.json crawler_url_coverage, Cloudflare GraphQL by user agent
kpis.why: Googlebot fetched robots.txt 4x and sitemap.xml 7x in the same window and then crawled 2 pages. It is declining, not blocked.

kpis.name: ClaudeBot URL coverage
kpis.how: data/traffic.json crawler_url_coverage
kpis.why: Assistant crawlers have this catalogue even though Google does not. This is the discovery channel that is actually working.

kpis.name: Human requests, storefront (assets included)
kpis.how: data/traffic.json human_evidence.requests_render_proven. Requests, not page views: it counts every asset fetch too. The page-view figure behind it is 218 in 7 days, 64 excluding the home page, spread over 49 of the other 311 URLs, with 109 URLs drawing nothing from any browser-shaped agent (docs/TRAFFIC_R1.md). 33 of 124 browser-shaped UA strings passed the render test.
kpis.why: The honest size of the audience. A spoofed UA that never loads an asset is not a person.

kpis.name: GitHub unique visitors
kpis.how: gh api repos/theluckystrike/mcp-servers/traffic/views
kpis.why: The repo is the other front door. 0 stars, 0 forks and 0 watchers since 2026-09-02.

kpis.name: Release asset fetches (mostly automated)
kpis.how: gh api releases (scripts/measure.mjs). NOT an install count: across 597 assets the counts are near-uniform (mean 8.90, median 8, p10 6, p90 11, top 10 of 597 hold 5.7%), and obsolete releases score the same per asset as the current one. Human demand is a power law; this is machine sweeping. See docs/AUDIENCE_REALITY_R1.md.
kpis.why: Kept for continuity only. It was previously reported as an install metric against a target of 1,000 and read as met, which was wrong.

kpis.how: api.npmjs.org
kpis.why: npx is the default install path in every client guide; blocked on npm login.

kpis.why: Hosted use is the only kind directories and registries count.

kpis.name: Hosted downloads served

kpis.how: audits: truncated history, capped loops, partial files all fixed
kpis.why: A plausible wrong answer costs more than an error.

kpis.name: Checkout sessions from humans (last 100)
kpis.how: stripe checkout sessions list --live, metadata.probe absent
kpis.why: Validation probes create sessions too; only untagged ones are demand.

kpis.name: Paid sessions
kpis.how: stripe checkout sessions list --live payment_status
kpis.why: The number that matters.

kpis.name: License keys minted
kpis.how: wrangler kv key list --remote on LICENSES
kpis.why: One key per paid session; zero means no purchase reached /success.

kpis.name: Upgrade link clicks (humans, 7d)
kpis.how: GET https://mcp.zovo.one/stats/clicks, sum of by_src[*].last7d. WARNING: the worker guard is start-anchored, so any browser User-Agent is counted, including this project's own agents. docs/CONVERSION_R1.md measured 77.9% of clicks carrying a src no live page emits. Treat as an upper bound, never as human demand.
kpis.why: The click is the step between a cap message and a checkout session; without it a stalled funnel and a message nobody reads look the same.

kpis.name: Click to checkout-session ratio
kpis.how: 100 * checkout sessions from humans (last 100, Stripe) / upgrade link clicks (7d, /stats/clicks) - the two windows differ (last 100 ever vs last 7 days), so this is an approximation, not the true window-matched ratio
kpis.why: Separates whether people are seeing the link (clicks) from whether the checkout page itself converts (ratio); a link with clicks and no sessions points at the redirect or the Stripe page, not the message.

kpis.name: Pro tenants on hosted endpoints
kpis.how: Stripe-bound tenants (REMOTE_DATA bind: prefix, 0) plus distinct lic: tenant ids whose key the billing worker minted (LICENSES session:*, 0 keys). EXCLUDED: the 1585 raw lic: documents are per (key, server) pairs, not tenants (56 distinct ids), and 56 of those ids are validation probes signed locally by scripts/sign-license.mjs, never bought.
kpis.why: Real Pro usage on hosted. The old count read every lic: document, so one validation run over 16 servers looked like 16 paying tenants.
